learning_experiences: brainstorm on the meaning and importance of fire,
discuss the possible causes of fire outbreaks in the environment (flammable substances, electrical faults, combustible materials),
share experiences on ways of preventing fire outbreaks in the environment,
discuss firefighting techniques in the work environment, (cooling, smothering, starving, interrupting),
role play fire fighting techniques for extinguishing fire.
key_inquiry_questions: Why is fire safety important?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Critical Thinking and Problem Solving: learner acquires active listening and communication skills when following simple instructions to complete tasks while role-playing firefighting techniques in the work environment.
Creativity and Imagination: learner acquires networking skills by undertaking group activities and exchanging new ideas that inspire creative thinking skills during the role-play on firefighting techniques for extinguishing fire.
sub_strands.values:
Responsibility: learner engages in assigned roles and duties when role-playing firefighting techniques.
Respect: learner appreciates diverse opinions when brainstorming on the possible causes of fire outbreaks in the environment.
sub_strands.pcis: Safety: learner enhances safety awareness when sharing experiences on ways of preventing fire outbreaks in the environment.
sub_strands.links: Integrated Science: learner relates fire safety to fire control measures in Integrated Science.
sub_strands.design_notes: Second read left this for a person to confirm: lessons: table says 6, summary says 7.

outcomes.text: identify possible causes of fire outbreaks in the environment
explain ways of preventing fire outbreaks in the environment
extinguish fires in the environment using appropriate methods
acknowledge the need for fire safety in day-to-day life

learning_experiences: brainstorm on the meaning of data and information in an electronic device,
use available resources to search for the importance of data in electronic devices,
discuss threats to data in electronic devices (virus and unauthorised access),
discuss techniques of securing data in an electronic device (use passwords; and scan electronic devices using antivirus),
use appropriate techniques to secure data in an electronic device against possible threats.
key_inquiry_questions: How is data protected in an electronic device?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Critical Thinking and Problem Solving: learner acquires active listening and communication skills when discussing threats to data in electronic devices
Digital Literacy: learner acquires skills of interacting with technology when using digital devices to secure electronic data in a user environment.
sub_strands.values:
Responsibility: learner engages in assigned roles and duties when securing electronic data in the workplace against possible threats.
Respect: learner appreciates diverse opinions when brainstorming on the threats of electronic data in the work environment.
sub_strands.pcis: Cyber Security: learner enhances online safety when practising how to secure electronic data in the user environment.
sub_strands.links: Mathematics: learner relates data safety to data handling in mathematics.
sub_strands.design_notes: Second read left this for a person to confirm: lessons: table says 4, summary says 11.

outcomes.text: outline the importance of data in an electronic device
identify threats to data in an electronic device
describe ways of protecting data in an electronic device
secure data in an electronic device
acknowledge the need for data safety in day-to-day life

sub_strands.pcis: Social cohesion: learners work together harmoniously when discussing how to draw combined shapes.

learning_experiences: use print or digital media to search for information on plain scales,

use drawing instruments to construct a plain scale,

Responsibility: learner demonstrates self-drive when practicing drawing plane figures to a given plain scale.

sub_strands.links: Mathematics: learner relates skills of scale drawing to linear scale in Mathematics.

learning_experiences: brainstorm on the meaning of the terms ‘visual programming’ and ‘visual programming application,
use available resources to search for information on types of visual programming applications (Educational, Multimedia, Video games),
brainstorm on examples of visual programming applications (Microsoft MakeCode, Scratch, Sprite box),
launch and discuss the different features of visual programming applications (input, processing, output, effects such as sound, animations and background),

use available resources to search for information on terminologies used in visual programming (syntax, variables, input output statements, coding, coding blocks, sequence statement repeating statement, selection statement, variable declarations) and discuss with peers,
use visual programming software to create sequential instructions.
key_inquiry_questions: How are computer programs used in day-to-day life?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Communication and Collaboration: learner develops speaking, listening and team working skills when discussing the features of a visual programming application.
Critical Thinking and Problem Solving: learner develops open mindedness and creativity skills when applying effects such as sound, animations, and background in a program.
sub_strands.values: Responsibility: learner engages in assigned roles and duties when using visual programming software to create instructions in the work environment.
sub_strands.pcis: Peer Education: learner enhances healthy inter and intra-personal relationships with others when searching for information on terminologies used in visual programming and discussing with peers.
sub_strands.links: Creative Arts: learner relates visual programming skills to drawing of animations in creative arts.
sub_strands.design_notes: Second read left this for a person to confirm: lessons: table says 13, summary says 14.

outcomes.text: identify types of visual programming applications used in day-to-day life
explore the features of visual programming applications in a user environment
create instructions to solve problems using visual programming application
value the importance of visual programming in day-to-day life

sub_strands.values: Peace: learner portrays respect for diversity when visiting locality to explore the uses of composite materials.

visit the locality to explore the uses of ceramic materials,
use a chart to match ceramic materials to their uses in the work environment.

Unity: learner collaborates with others when using a chart to match ceramic materials with their use in the work environment.
sub_strands.pcis: Safety: learner observes safety precautions when investigating the physical properties of ceramic materials.
sub_strands.links: Creative Arts: learner enhances skills of pottery when identifying items made of ceramic materials.

learning_experiences: use available resources to identify cutting tools in the work environment (snips, chisels, handsaws, planes, hacksaws, scrappers, knives, strippers, cutters),
discuss the use of cutting tools in the work environment,
use audio visual aids to observe the use of cutting tools in the work environment,
demonstrate safe use of cutting tools to perform specific tasks,
carry out given tasks using cutting tools,
maintain and store cutting tools in the work environment.
key_inquiry_questions: Why are cutting tools cared for?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Learning to Learn: learner acquires the skill of working collaboratively with others when discussing the use of cutting tools in the work environment.
Critical Thinking and Problem Solving: learner acquires evaluation and decision-making skills when demonstrating safe use of cutting tools in performing specific tasks.
sub_strands.values:
Responsibility: learner observes safety precautions when using cutting tools available to perform given tasks.
Unity: learner respects other people’s opinions when discussing the use of cutting tools in the work environment.
sub_strands.pcis: Safety: learner observes safety when demonstrating safe use of cutting tools to perform specific tasks.
sub_strands.links: Agriculture: learner relates the use of cutting tools to farm and kitchen tools.

outcomes.text: identify cutting tools used in the work environment
select cutting tools for given tasks in a workplace
use cutting tools to perform a given task
care for cutting tools in the work environment
recognise the importance of cutting tools in the work environment

learning_experiences: brainstorm on the meaning of the term ‘computer software’ and present to peers,

perform tasks using different application software (word processing, presentation, spreadsheet).
key_inquiry_questions: How is computer software used in day-to-day life?
Why is computer software important?

sub_strands.values: Integrity: learner exhibits fairness by giving equal opportunities to peers when brainstorming functions of application software.
sub_strands.pcis: Peer Education and Mentorship: learner develops interpersonal relationships while they brainstorm on the functions of different application software.

learning_experiences: brainstorm and present the meaning of basic terms used in bookkeeping,
discuss the importance of bookkeeping for a business,
calculate assets, liabilities and capital using the bookkeeping equation,
read and analyse a case study on cash and credit transactions,
determine the cost and price of a given product to calculate profit and loss,
discuss the components of a statement of financial position, cash flow and income statement,
draw and present simple statements of financial position, cash flow and income statement for a business.
key_inquiry_questions: Why is bookkeeping important to a business?
How are the statements of financial position, cash flow and income statement prepared?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Critical Thinking and Problem-Solving: learner acquires evaluation and decision-making skills when calculating assets, liabilities and capital using the bookkeeping equation.
Self-efficacy: learner develops effective communication skills when discussing, presenting and preparing statements of financial position, cash flow and income.
sub_strands.values:
Peace: learner works harmoniously with members of the team when brainstorming and presenting the meaning of basic terms used in bookkeeping.
Responsibility: learner performs tasks assigned when calculating assets, liabilities and capital using the bookkeeping equation.
Respect: learner shows regard for the input of every member of the team when discussing the components of a statement of financial position, cash flow and income statement.
sub_strands.pcis: Financial Literacy: learner enhances bookkeeping skills when drawing and presenting simple statements of financial position, cash flow and income statement for a business.
sub_strands.links: Mathematics: learner enhances skills of mathematical operations when calculating values for assets, liabilities and capital.

outcomes.text: explain the importance of bookkeeping in entrepreneurship
classify business transactions in bookkeeping
prepare simple financial statements for a business
appreciate the importance of financial records in day-to-day life

search from available resources the role of intermediaries in distribution of goods and services to the consumer,
search and watch video clips on channels for distributing different goods and services,
prepare a chart on channels for distribution of different goods and services,
read and discuss stories on different distribution channels for goods and services,
debate on ethical and unethical practices on distribution of goods and services.

Digital Literacy: learner acquires the skills of interacting with digital devices when watching and listening to video clips on channels for distributing goods and services.

Respect: learner develops regard for self and others when discussing the meaning of channels of distribution and role of intermediaries in the distribution of goods and services.
Peace: learner displays tolerance and respect for others when debating on ethical issues on distribution of goods and services.

indicators.indicator: Ability to extinguish fires in the environment using appropriate methods. Ability to describe ways of protecting data in an electronic device.

levels.EE: Extinguishes fires in the environment using four appropriate methods. Comprehensively describes ways of protecting data in an electronic device.
levels.ME: Extinguishes fires in the environment using three appropriate methods. Describes ways of protecting data in an electronic device.
levels.AE: Extinguishes fires in the environment using two appropriate methods. Describes some of the ways of protecting data in an electronic device.
levels.BE: Extinguishes fires in the environment using only one appropriate method. Describes a few ways of protecting data in an electronic device.

indicators.indicator: Ability to identify instruments used in drawing.

levels.EE: Identifies four instruments used in drawing.
levels.ME: Identifies three instruments used in drawing.
levels.AE: Identifies two instruments used in drawing.
levels.BE: Identifies one instrument used in drawing.

indicators.indicator: Ability to draw lines used for dimensioning in drawing.

levels.EE: Draws lines used for dimensioning in drawing with exceptional clarity.
levels.ME: Draws lines used for dimensioning in drawing.
levels.AE: Draws lines used for dimensioning in drawing with few unclear details.
levels.BE: Draws lines used for dimensioning in drawing with many unclear details

indicators.indicator: Ability to describe the features of a plain scale used in drawing Ability to create instructions to solve problems using visual programming application.

levels.EE: Describes the features of a plain scale used in drawing with illustrations Proficiently creates instructions to solve problems using visual programming application.
levels.ME: Describes the features of a plain scale used in drawing Creates instructions to solve problems using visual programming application.
levels.AE: Describes some features of a plain scale used in drawing Creates some instructions to solve problems using visual programming application.
levels.BE: Describes a few features of a plain scale used in drawing. Creates a few instructions to solve problems using visual programming application.

indicators.indicator: Ability to describe the composition of composite materials in the locality. Ability to describe physical properties of ceramic materials in the locality. Ability to relate ceramic materials to their use in a work environment.

levels.EE: Describes the composition of composite materials in the locality with illustrations. Describes five physical properties of ceramic materials in the locality. Relates ceramic materials to their use in a work environment citing examples.
levels.ME: Describes the composition of composite materials in the locality. Describes four physical properties of ceramic materials in the locality. Relates ceramic materials to their use in a work environment.
levels.AE: Describes the composition of most of the composite materials in the locality. Describes two or three physical properties of ceramic materials in the locality. Relates some ceramic materials to their use in a work environment.
levels.BE: Describes the composition of only a few of the composite materials in the locality. Describes one physical property of ceramic materials in the locality. Relates ceramic materials to their uses in a work environment, with guidance.

indicators.indicator: Ability to identify cutting tools used in the work environment. Ability to explain the functions of different application software in the workplace. Ability to use computer software to perform tasks in day-to-day life.

levels.EE: Identifies more than five cutting tools used in the work environment. Explains the functions of different application software in the workplace with illustrations. Proficiently uses computer software to perform tasks in day-to-day life.
levels.ME: Identifies five cutting tools used in the work environment. Explains the functions of different application software in the workplace. Uses computer software to perform tasks in day-to-day life.
levels.AE: Identifies four or three cutting tools used in the work environment. Explains some of the functions of different application software in the workplace. Uses computer software to perform some of the tasks in day-to-day life.
levels.BE: Identifies less than 3 cutting tools used in the work environment. Explains a few of the functions of different application software in the workplace. Uses computer software to perform a few of the tasks in day-to-day life.

indicators.indicator: Ability to classify business transactions in bookkeeping. Ability to prepare simple financial statements for a business. Ability to explain the importance of budgeting in day-to-day life.

levels.EE: Classifies two business transactions in bookkeeping, citing examples. Prepares a detailed financial statements for a business. Explains the importance of budgeting in day-to-day life in detail.
levels.ME: Classifies two business transactions in bookkeeping. Prepares a simple financial statements for a business. Explains the importance of budgeting in day-to-day life.
levels.AE: Classifies one business transactions in bookkeeping. Prepares a simple financial statements for a business, leaving out few details. Explains the importance of budgeting in day-to-day life, leaving out a few details.
levels.BE: Classifies one business transactions in bookkeeping, with prompt. Prepares a simple financial statement for a business, leaving out many details. Explains the importance of budgeting in day-to-day life, leaving out many details.
